findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the marker-block pairing algorithm for repeated/interleaved markers (e.g. each `<<<END>>>` pairs with the nearest preceding unmatched `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>`; a trailing unmatched open is ignored so long as >=1 complete block exists) and pin it.
evidence: Plan pins single-block, multi-block (last-wins), and unterminated-open (markerless) cases, but not repeated-open or open-after-final-close cases.
The scanned text (and therefore the selected payload) is determined by which spans count as blocks; a greedy vs. stack vs. non-greedy pairing gives different concatenated regions.
The whole premise is removing extraction ambiguity, so the pairing algorithm is load-bearing, not incidental.
findings.finding: The 'complete marker block' pairing rule is under-specified for repeated or interleaved markers: the plan defines a block only as 'a `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>` followed by a later `<<<END>>>`' and does not state how overlapping opens (OPEN...OPEN...END) or an open-after-close-with-no-final-close (OPEN...END...OPEN) are paired.
findings.location: Approach — 'one or more COMPLETE marker blocks (a `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>` followed by a later `<<<END>>>`)'
scenarios: A model emits `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>> {draft} <<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>> {final} <<<END>>>` (nested/repeated open) — which region(s) are scanned?
A model emits a complete block then a trailing dangling `<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>` with no closing `<<<END>>>` — is the earlier complete block still honored, or does the dangling open void the whole reply?
